name: Mnemorin
subcategory: memory replay compound / experiential recapture agent
description: Mnemorin is a hippocampal activation compound that, when combined with a user's BCI memory index, allows the full re-experiencing of archived episodic memories with near-perfect fidelity — emotions, sensations, and context included. Users relive chosen memories not as passive recollection but as complete immersive re-entry. Lazarus positions it as a grief therapy tool; the recreational market uses it for something closer to addiction.
effects: Complete immersive re-entry into chosen memories
Full emotional and sensory fidelity of the original experience
Temporary elimination of present-tense anxiety and dissatisfaction
Sense of accessing something true and permanent
side_effects: Reality dissatisfaction syndrome — present life feels pale and insufficient
Memory distortion with repeated replay — the drug enhances emotional content over time, making memories more perfect than they were
Inability to form new positive memories that compete with replayed ones
In extreme cases, users lose the ability to distinguish memory-state from present-state
duration: Subjective hours (real-time: 90 minutes to 3 hours depending on dose)
cultural_context: Mnemorin addiction is GLMZ's quiet epidemic — it affects mostly Tier 3 and Tier 4 adults who are old enough to have significant memory archives. Grief counselors, divorce attorneys, and the bereaved are the most vulnerable demographics. Support groups exist under the name 'Amber Circles.' Among the ultra-elite in Tier 5, custom memory curation services pair Mnemorin with professionally edited memory archives — people pay to re-experience their best moments perfected.
story_hooks: A detective investigating a string of deaths discovers the victims were all Mnemorin users who had been replaying a specific shared memory — one that shouldn't exist, featuring a location none of them ever visited

A Mnemorin-addicted woman has been replaying the same afternoon for two years and has begun referring to it in present tense — her family hires a runner to find out if Lazarus's neural-direct formula has caused structural memory damage, or something worse
A Tier 5 memory curation studio has been caught selling composite memories — constructed experiences built from multiple donors — and one of those memories contains evidence of a crime
